In doing so, you will be awarded prestigious Golden Carrots, a sure way to outclass your eternal rival! Purchase the buildings that best suit your strategy and place them in the best locations to grow your districts and earn more and more Golden Carrots. Unless, of course, you choose the exact location your opponent had their eye on, thwarting all their expansion plans! Finally, the inhabitants will send you their requests, which will guide you in your construction choices and can bring in a lot of a lot of extra Golden Carrots! A high replayability awaits you, as not all buildings will be available and you will never draw the same Request cards twice! Contents 1 Overview and Aim of the Game 2 Setup 2.1 Setup Cards 3 The round 3.1 Preparing a new round 3.2 The turn 3.2.1 Plan (mandatory) 3.2.2 Construct (optional) 3.2.2.1 Placing a Building 3.2.2.2 Activating a Neighborhood 3.2.2.3 Building triggers 3.2.2.4 Calculating the influence of a Neighborhood 3.2.2.5 Constructing additional Buildings 3.2.3 Create (optional) 3.3 End of the turn 4 End of the round 5 End of the game 6 Credits Overview and Aim of the Game Bunny Kingdom: Town is a tile-drafting and placement game played over 4 rounds. During each round, you'll be planning and constructing new Buildings to develop the Neighborhoods under your control. Choose your construction plans carefully to boost your strategy, but watch out: those you overlook could be just what your opponent needs! Each new Building you construct will bring you resources or increase your influence. Don't forget to satisfy the requests of your new townsfolk, which will remain secret until the end of the game and could completely change the outcome. During final scoring, the player with the most Golden Carrots is the winner! Setup At the start of the game, Upgrade Tiles are randomly drawn until the total cost totals 8 or more. Each player starts the game with 2 Coins. The initial bridges and plot cards are set up based on the game's chosen Setup Card. Setup Cards When setting up a game, you can choose a Setup Card (or select a random one). These determine which plots are initially available (the spaces where you can build your building) and where the game's bridges will be placed. Card Choose For Plots and Bridges 1: A Golden Opportunity First game Starting Plots and Bridges 2: New arrivals A game with spread-out plots Starting Plots and Bridges 3: At the forest's edge A high-wood game Starting Plots and Bridges 4: By the water Initial plots along the river Starting Plots and Bridges 5: On the other side of the river A game with no bridges Starting Plots (no Bridges) 6: Beyond the horizon A random setup Starting Plots are randomly drawn. Players place 1 Bridge each. The round A game of Bunny Kingdom: Town is played over 4 rounds , with each player taking turns being the first player. Each round consists of a series of player turns , continuing until all available Building tiles have been taken. Preparing a new round At the start of each new round, complete the following steps. Each player receives 2 Coins from the reserve. (You received 3 during setup, so you'll start the first round with 5.) Reveal the first 5 tiles from the Building pile and place them on the designated spaces on the board. These are the Buildings you can construct during this round. Each player draws 2 Request cards and chooses 1 which they place face down in front of them. Place the unchosen cards into the discard pile face-up. You can now begin the round. [Rating: 2/10] The game is hugely unbalanced. I’ve played it 3 times and each time the difference in points was over 100 points. So if you’re ahead at the beginning you’ll surely win the game. Will never play it again.

[Rating: 3/10] Just played 1 game on BGA. It's what it is... feel like the game Donuts, with pimped up tiles, instead of colorful Donuts.

[Rating: 4/10] It's okay for a quick version of bunny kingdom. Pieces could be better, why isn't the board double sided with a different map and the player powers being limited is stupid. I don't like the player power system, carrot cards too lucky and not worth enough. From first play the first player gets a definite big advantage, the 2nd player should get an extra coin(s) or something. Really unbalanced, feels like it wasn't play tested enough.

[Rating: 4/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  I would prefer to just play the original. This plays fast and works just fine, but I don't find it nearly as enjoyable. There is room for clever play despite the luck of the draw.

[Rating: 4/10] Meh - You both kinda do your own thing on different sides of the map because both players want to connect to their own buildings.

[Rating: 5/10] Play - 2 times  Love the art, but a lot of things feel uncontrollable. The request cards, plot cards, and building cards depend too much on luck, so it’s hard to plan anything strategically. I’m still deciding whether to sell it or not.

[Rating: 5/10] It's fine for what it is but I'd frankly much prefer playing the original Bunny Kingdom even at two players.  It's just a much more interesting game for me.

[Rating: 5/10] Ok, I can see why I would play this over Kingdomino SOMETIMES. The random request cards, the random draw is very addictive. But the game feels WAY too mean for what it is - denying things for your opponent is very frequently the best move. The snowballing nature of building and the random draw of the plots really produces "win more" scenarios.  Similar to: * Imperial Settlers - the art and the region building aspect sort of feels similar * Pax Pamir - like in 2p Pax, you're holding onto your cards and then BURST to WIN. * Kingdomino - the whole icon*stars calculation is similar to region size 

[Rating: 5/10] There's so much potential here; love the resource balance, love the plot selection mechanism, and the area scoring is interesting... But... Every game we play the score boils down to being more than 50% reliant on hidden information your opponent has no way of interacting with. In a two player game that's just no fun. Perhaps if you knew the game really well, you could guess what objectives folks are shooting for and trying to block, but there's not enough actions to do that while also securing your own.
